AI watermark status: not assessed. Invisible characters and document properties have many ordinary causes. Their presence or absence cannot establish AI authorship or a statistical watermark.

1. Choose your source

Paste text or open UTF-8 .txt, .md, or .docx (10 MB max). Inspecting creates a separate working copy. Your uploaded file is never overwritten.

Text, Markdown, or Word · Up to 10 MB

Pasting cannot reveal the original file’s metadata. DOCX support extracts text for inspection; revised exports are text, not formatted Word files.

2. Technical inspection

Metadata & coverage
Only selected findings with a proposed replacement change the copy. Joiners, direction controls, and variation selectors are report-only to preserve scripts and emoji. This is a bounded inspection, not a universal steganography scan.


Additional server inspection
Optional server inspection sends the last inspected original document through this site's service to watermark-remover. Your writing guide is not sent. Local checks and downloads work without this service.
Not run. No document has been sent.
Report only. No rewriting or cleanup endpoint is called. Upstream labels such as “suspicious” are technical findings, not proof of AI authorship.
3. Optional style review
Monthly digest register (§6). These are editorial choices, not evidence of AI authorship. Exact em-dash checks work on any text; the other suggestions are a human-reviewed pass on this newsletter, shown only while their source passages still match. Semantic checks are not automated.
Read the supplied guide and review coverage
Bundled review baseline: Version 2.3, July 20, 2026. Newsletter review: cadence, repetition and vocabulary suggestions below; no blanket “we” replacement because the draft identifies Sarah and the author. The orientation-document Ask pass does not apply. No automatic grammar score, aphorism count, or fact verification is claimed.


4. Review the changes
Original text is held separately. Red is removed; green is added. Unusual characters appear as ⟦U+XXXX⟧ in this view so invisible changes are visible. Downloads retain actual characters.


About this prototype and watermark-remover
The repository’s Unicode cleanup can identify concrete character properties; those are not proof of where text came from. Its statistical detector integrations require matching schemes/configurations or keys. Rewriting and lexical divergence do not demonstrate that an arbitrary vendor watermark has been removed. Its cleanup endpoint also includes a rewriting stage, making it a poor default for preserving your voice.
This prototype uses its own small inspection engine. The optional additional inspection calls watermark-remover through a configured server. It does not call an AI model or statistical detector. No automatic normalization, homoglyph substitution, or prose rewrite is performed.
